additional_info.subject: Description
additional_info.body:
We observed delay in the SoC transmission from the charger to the OCPP backend.
Scenario:
The EV starts charging, and SoC values begin updating on the HMI screen.
However, the same data reaches the backend and user interface after approximately 30-45 seconds.
Expected Behavior:
The SoC value should be transmitted to the OCPP backend synchronously or with a delay of no more than a few seconds after it appears on the HMI.
As suggested, we have set the MeterValueSampleInterval to 10 seconds on the CPO side.
However, there is no change in the behavior. As you can see in the logs at the attachment, the first MeterValues message is sent around 30 seconds after the charging session starts, and afterwards it continues to be sent every 30 seconds.
Charging start:
2026-01-13T19:01:21.688 – Charging phase changed to P06_CHARGE
Internal charger measurements (SOC etc. are already available in real time):
2026-01-13T19:01:23.176: DC2: |EVSE_MaxPwr[kW]=40|EVSE_MaxCur[A]=64|EVSE_NowPwr[kW]=11.4|EVSE_NowCur[A]=29|EVSE_NowVol[V]=392.5 .......
First MeterValues sent to OCPP:
2026-01-13T
19:01:52
.320: OCPP: Send command: MeterValues (eb38903e-e2c2-4b23-9a7f-9176bba62639) - {"connectorId":2,"transactionId":63763159,"meterValue":....
Second MeterValues:
2026-01-13T
19:02:22
.319: OCPP: Send command: MeterValues (2c89ba54-35c5-480d-a801-776c1e8dc3ce) - {"connectorId":2,"transactionId":63763159,"meterValue":....
Based on the current logs, MeterValues are still being sent with a fixed 30-second interval even though MeterValueSampleInterval is set to 10.
From your experience with SichargeD and OCPP, what would you suggest as the next step to identify what is enforcing this 30-second behavior?

additional_info.subject: 0474427 - ID0474427-DC/Si-D/TR-[Y2/T4 314241502023] Delay in SoC Transmission CRM:00314000257
additional_info.body:
Dear Emre-abi,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0474427.
The ticket has been opened to report that the MeterValues are sent to the charger every 30 seconds, even though the MeterValueSampleInterval key was configured to 10 seconds in the Backend.
I had a look at the logs you reported, and these are my findings:
On 2025-01-13, a charging session was stopped at 2026-01-13T10:28:26.
At 2026-01-13T10:28:50 the charger received ChangeConfiguration request from the Backend, which was accepted:
2026-01-13T10:28:50.304977+00:00 [FW080005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/89db40bccee3[826]: OCPP: Received command: ChangeConfiguration (24087861-de15-43b8-9d8f-c7c299d8718a) - {"key":"MeterValueSampleInterval","value":"10"}
2026-01-13T10:28:50.309692+00:00 [FW080005G1] sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/89db40bccee3[826]: OCPP: Send result: ChangeConfiguration (24087861-de15-43b8-9d8f-c7c299d8718a) - {"status":"Accepted"}
After the change of OCPP configuration key, no further charging session has been attempted.
At 2026-01-13T11:07:18, we experience some subsequent unusual requests from the Backend:
The Backend asked for #4 times (in orange) to get the value of the key "GetConfigurationMaxKeys", and we provide the value.
The Backend asked for #4 times (in blue)  to get the values of several configuration keys, including the MeterValueSampleInterval, and we provide the values. We can see that for MeterValueSampleInterval the value was 10.
The Backend asked for #3 times (in yellow) to change the value of MeterValueSampleInterval back to 30, and we reply with Accepted.
As a consequence, in the charging session you reported at 2026-01-13T19:01:23, the MeterValues are sent every 30 seconds because the Backend had previously set the MeterValueSampleInterval Configuration Key back to 30 seconds.
Right now, the MeterValueSampleInterval is also 30 seconds:
From the charger point of view, I do not see anything wrong. Attached to this email you will find the logs as reference.
For sure, what seems odd to me are the multiple, nearly instantaneous, requests coming from the Backend. In my opinion, it seems nearly like the Backend has a default set of all the OCPP Configuration keys, and periodically it checks with the charger what is its current set of OCPP Configuration keys, and if any differs from the default set, the Backend changes it back.
This is purely an assumption from my side. I would recommend to reach out to the OCPP Backend and ask for clarification in regards of this change of the MeterValueSampleInterval from their side.
Please let me know if further support is required. Looking forward to hearing feedback from you soon.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
